arms.predicted: Multi-start NN construction + NN-list 2-opt with cycling detection + linked-list or-opt will score higher than the iter-2 baseline of 76.3 on the judge, improving on the 6 currently-failing test cases.
arms.observed: Judge SCORE: 76.31 (clean run), 75.85, 73.86, 70.74 (system-load-affected runs). Local per-test-case analysis: average 76.26%. Per-test-case comparison vs control: TC4 +0.33% (multi-start finds marginally better tour for N=1000), TC6 -0.36% (slight regression), TC7 -0.54% (slight regression), all other TCs identical. The multi-start, cycling detection, and or-opt combination does NOT improve over the iter-2 baseline. The judge score under stable conditions (76.31) is within noise of the control (76.29). Earlier low scores (73.86, 70.74) were due to system load causing TLE on time-sensitive test cases.
arms.diagnostic_note: Three mechanisms were tested in combination: (1) Multi-start NN construction for N<=5000 — converges to equivalent-quality local optima, net neutral. (2) Cycling detection — breaks 2-opt cycling on grid data (TC6) but doesn't improve tour quality, only saves wasted time. (3) Or-opt (single-city relocation using NN-list candidates) — finds no improving moves after 2-opt convergence. The combination has no synergy because each component is individually neutral. The 2-opt local optimum quality is a hard ceiling for these neighborhoods. Breaking through requires fundamentally different move types (3-opt, LK moves) or construction heuristics that exploit problem-specific data structure.

arms.diagnostic_note: Judge score is stable at 76.288 when system load is low. The 5-point drops correspond to individual test cases timing out under load — the algorithm's time-dependent 2-opt converges so late on large N test cases that even small system load fluctuations can cause TLE.

discrepancy_analysis: h-main REFUTED: the combination of multi-start NN + cycling detection + or-opt scores 76.26-76.31, essentially identical to the iter-2 baseline of 76.29. The directional prediction (improvement) was wrong — the score is flat. Error type is 'magnitude' because the predicted improvement direction was correct (slightly positive at +0.02 points) but the magnitude is negligible (within measurement noise). Per-test-case analysis reveals: (a) multi-start for TC4 (N=1000) provides +0.33% improvement, (b) or-opt provides no improvements after 2-opt convergence, (c) cycling detection saves time on TC6 but doesn't improve tour quality. The 2-opt local optimum quality is a hard ceiling that multi-start, or-opt, and cycling detection cannot overcome. h-control-negative CONFIRMED: stable at 76.288 under low system load.
